source.text: וְאִשָּׁ֣ה אַחַ֣ת מִנְּשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־הַ֠נְּבִיאִים צָעֲקָ֨ה אֶל־אֱלִישָׁ֜ע לֵאמֹ֗ר עַבְדְּךָ֤ אִישִׁי֙ מֵ֔ת וְאַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ כִּ֣י עַבְדְּךָ֔ הָיָ֥ה יָרֵ֖א אֶת־יְהוָ֑ה וְהַ֨נֹּשֶׁ֔ה בָּ֗א לָקַ֜חַת אֶת־שְׁנֵ֧י יְלָדַ֛י ל֖וֹ לַעֲבָדִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And a woman, one of [the] wives of [the] sons of the prophets, cried out to Elisha, saying, Your servant, my husband, [is] dead, and you know that your servant was fearing Yahweh; and the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves.

en.L: And a woman from the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, saying, "Your servant, my husband, is dead, and you know that your servant feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."
en.B: The wife of a man from the company of prophets cried out to Elisha, "My husband, your servant, has died, and you know that your servant feared {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Now the man he owed money to has come to take my two children as his slaves."
en.R: A woman whose husband had been one of the group of prophets cried out to Elisha for help. She said, "My husband, your servant, has died. You know how he honored and obeyed {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. But now a man my husband owed money to has come to take my two boys away to be his slaves."

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: members of a community of prophets
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means members of a group, not children. Such groups of prophets lived at Bethel, Jericho and Gilgal (2 Kings 2:3, 5, 15; 4:38) and looked to Elisha as their leader (6:1). Some of them, like this woman's husband, were married and had families.

decisions.choice: your servant: a humble way of speaking of her husband as Elisha's loyal follower
decisions.reason: Speaking of someone as "your servant" to a person of higher standing was the polite way to address him (Genesis 18:3; 1 Samuel 20:7-8). It reminds Elisha that the dead man belonged to his own circle.

decisions.choice: feared the LORD: lived in reverence and obedience toward Yahweh
decisions.reason: To fear Yahweh is to honor him and keep his ways (Deuteronomy 10:12). She names her husband's faithfulness as the ground of her appeal: a godly man's family is now about to be broken up.

decisions.choice: the creditor came to take her children as slaves: enslavement for debt
decisions.reason: A family that could not pay a debt could lose its children to the lender as slaves until the debt was worked off. The law limited this and required release for Israelites (Exodus 21:2-7; Leviticus 25:39-43; Deuteronomy 15:12), but the prophets show how harshly it was used (Amos 2:6; Nehemiah 5:5). For a widow, losing her sons meant losing her only support.

decisions.choice: slaves (every level)
decisions.reason: Here the children are to be taken as property in payment of a debt, so enslavement itself is the point. Following the style guide, "slave" stays at every level instead of "servant".

decisions.choice: company of prophets (Balanced); group of prophets (Readable)
decisions.reason: These are the book-wide wordings for "sons of the prophets". Balanced and Readable also make clear that her husband was the member of the group.

decisions.choice: honored and obeyed
decisions.reason: Readable explains "feared" by what it meant in practice, so a young reader does not think he was afraid of God.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלֶ֤יהָ אֱלִישָׁע֙ מָ֣ה אֶֽעֱשֶׂה־לָּ֔ךְ הַגִּ֣ידִי לִ֔י מַה־יֶּשׁ־לָ֖ךְ בַּבָּ֑יִת וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אֵ֣ין לְשִׁפְחָתְךָ֥ כֹל֙ בַּבַּ֔יִת כִּ֖י אִם־אָס֥וּךְ שָֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said to her Elisha, What shall I do for you? Tell me, what is there to you in the house? And she said, There is not to your maidservant anything in the house except a flask of oil.

en.L: And Elisha said to her, "What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?" And she said, "Your maidservant has nothing at all in the house except a flask of oil."
en.B: Elisha said to her, "What can I do for you? Tell me, what is there in your house?" She replied, "Your servant has nothing at all in the house, except a small jar of oil."
en.R: Elisha asked her, "How can I help you? Tell me, what do you have at home?" She answered, "I have nothing in the house except a little jar of olive oil."

decisions.choice: a flask of oil: a small container of oil
decisions.reason: The word appears only here. It seems to come from a verb meaning to pour oil on or anoint, so it was probably a small flask of oil for the skin, not a storage jar. Either way she has almost nothing.

decisions.choice: your maidservant: a humble way of saying "I"
decisions.reason: A woman speaking to someone of higher standing called herself "your maidservant" (1 Samuel 1:16; 25:24). She speaks as a petitioner.

decisions.choice: you: an older written form of the feminine "you", read in the usual way
decisions.reason: In this chapter the written Hebrew several times keeps an older spelling of the feminine "you" and "your" (here and in verses 3, 7, 16 and 23), and the traditional reading gives the usual form. The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: your servant (Balanced); I (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the polite self-reference as "your servant"; "maidservant" sounds dated. Readable says simply "I".

decisions.choice: olive oil
decisions.reason: The oil of Israel was olive oil; Readable names it, as 1 Kings 17:12 does.

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִ֨י שַׁאֲלִי־לָ֤ךְ כֵּלִים֙ מִן־הַח֔וּץ מֵאֵ֖ת כָּל־שְׁכֵנָ֑יִךְכֵּלִ֥ים רֵקִ֖ים אַל־תַּמְעִֽיטִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Go, borrow for yourself vessels from the outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not make few.

en.L: And he said, "Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside, from all your neighbors, empty vessels; do not get [only] a few.
en.B: He said, "Go around and borrow containers from all your neighbors, empty ones, and not just a few.
en.R: Elisha said, "Go to all your neighbors and borrow empty jars from them. Get as many as you can.

decisions.choice: vessels: containers of any kind
decisions.reason: The word covers any jar, pot or bowl. She is to collect whatever empty containers her neighbors can lend.

decisions.choice: do not make few: gather many
decisions.reason: The command looks ahead to verse 6: the oil flows as long as there are containers, so how many she gathers will set the size of the gift.

decisions.choice: Get as many as you can
decisions.reason: Readable turns the negative command into a plain positive one with the same sense.

source.text: וּבָ֗את וְסָגַ֤רְתְּ הַדֶּ֨לֶת֙ בַּעֲדֵ֣ךְ וּבְעַד־בָּנַ֔יִךְ וְיָצַ֕קְתְּ עַ֥ל כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְהַמָּלֵ֖א תַּסִּֽיעִי׃

records.literal_gloss: And go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and pour into all these vessels, and the full set aside.

en.L: Then go in and shut the door behind you and behind your sons, and pour into all these vessels, and set aside the full [ones]."
en.B: Then go inside with your sons and shut the door behind you. Pour oil into all these containers, and as each one is filled, set it aside."
en.R: Then go into your house with your sons and shut the door. Pour oil from your jar into all the empty jars. Each time one is full, put it to one side."

decisions.choice: shut the door: the miracle happens in private
decisions.reason: The gift is not a public show. The door is shut on the neighbors and on the creditor, and the family alone sees it, as Elisha later shuts the door when he prays for the dead boy (verse 33).

decisions.choice: pour: the oil from her flask
decisions.reason: The thing poured is not named, but it can only be the oil of verse 2.

decisions.choice: pour oil
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what she pours; Readable adds "from your jar".

source.text: וַתֵּ֨לֶךְ֙ מֵֽאִתּ֔וֹ וַתִּסְגֹּ֣ר הַדֶּ֔לֶת בַּעֲדָ֖הּ וּבְעַ֣ד בָּנֶ֑יהָ הֵ֛ם מַגִּשִׁ֥ים אֵלֶ֖יהָ וְהִ֥יא מוֹצָֽקֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons; they [were] bringing near to her, and she [was] pouring.

en.L: And she went from him and shut the door behind her and behind her sons. They were bringing [the vessels] to her, and she was pouring.
en.B: So she left him and shut the door behind her and her sons. They kept bringing the containers to her, and she kept pouring.
en.R: So she left Elisha and went home. She shut the door behind her and her sons. Her sons kept bringing jars to her, and she kept pouring oil into them.

decisions.choice: bringing ... pouring: action that went on and on
decisions.reason: Both verbs describe ongoing action. The sons kept bringing containers and their mother kept pouring, one after another.

decisions.choice: kept bringing ... kept pouring
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "kept" for the ongoing action, and Readable names the jars and the oil.

source.text: וַיְהִ֣י׀כִּמְלֹ֣את הַכֵּלִ֗ים וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶל־בְּנָהּ֙ הַגִּ֨ישָׁה אֵלַ֥י עוֹד֙ כֶּ֔לִי וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלֶ֔יהָ אֵ֥ין ע֖וֹד כֶּ֑לִי וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֖ד הַשָּֽׁמֶן׃

records.literal_gloss: And it happened, when were full the vessels, and she said to her son, Bring near to me yet a vessel. And he said to her, There is not yet a vessel. And stood the oil.

en.L: And it happened, when the vessels were full, that she said to her son, "Bring me another vessel." And he said to her, "There is not another vessel." And the oil stopped.
en.B: When the containers were all full, she told her son, "Bring me another one." But he told her, "There are no more." Then the oil stopped flowing.
en.R: When all the jars were full, she said to one of her sons, "Bring me another jar." But he told her, "There are no more jars." Then the oil stopped flowing.

decisions.choice: the oil stopped: the supply matched the containers she had gathered
decisions.reason: The oil did not run out; it stopped when there was nothing left to fill. The limit was set by the vessels, not by the gift (see verse 3).

decisions.choice: oil that keeps flowing: like the widow's jug in Elijah's day
decisions.reason: Elijah had provided for a widow and her son through a jug of oil that did not run out (1 Kings 17:14-16). Elisha, who received Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:15), does a like work for another widow.

decisions.choice: her son: one of the two sons
decisions.reason: The singular means whichever son was bringing the next container.

decisions.choice: stopped flowing
decisions.reason: The verb means "stood still"; "flowing" says what stopped.

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֗א וַתַּגֵּד֙ לְאִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְכִי֙ מִכְרִ֣י אֶת־הַשֶּׁ֔מֶן וְשַׁלְּמִ֖י אֶת־נִשְׁיֵ֑ךְ וְאַ֣תְּ וּבָנַ֔יִךְ תִֽחְיִ֖י בַּנּוֹתָֽר׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And she came and told the man of God, and he said, Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you [and] your sons will live on the remainder.

en.L: And she came and told the man of God. And he said, "Go, sell the oil and pay your debt, and you and your sons will live on what is left."
en.B: She came and told the man of God. He said, "Go and sell the oil, and pay off your debt. You and your sons can live on the rest."
en.R: She went and told Elisha, the man of God. He said, "Go and sell the oil. Pay back what you owe. Then you and your sons can live on the money that is left."

decisions.choice: the man of God: Elisha, as a prophet
decisions.reason: "Man of God" is a title for a prophet who speaks and acts for God (1 Kings 17:18, 24). The chapter uses it for Elisha again and again.

decisions.choice: you and your sons: the traditional reading adds "and"
decisions.reason: The written text has "you, your sons", and the traditional reading adds "and", with older spellings of "your" as in verse 2. The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: the gift pays the debt and keeps the family free
decisions.reason: The oil covers the debt, so the sons are not taken as slaves, and what is left supports the family.

decisions.choice: Elisha, the man of God; the money that is left
decisions.reason: Readable names Elisha once with his title, and says plainly that they will live on the money from the oil.

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י הַיּ֜וֹם וַיַּעֲבֹ֧ר אֱלִישָׁ֣ע אֶל־שׁוּנֵ֗ם וְשָׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֔ה וַתַּחֲזֶק־בּ֖וֹ לֶאֱכָל־לָ֑חֶם וַֽיְהִי֙ מִדֵּ֣י עָבְר֔וֹ יָסֻ֥ר שָׁ֖מָּה לֶאֱכָל־לָֽחֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it happened one day, and passed over Elisha to Shunem, and there [was] a great woman, and she took hold on him to eat bread; and it was, as often as he passed, he turned aside there to eat bread.

en.L: And it happened one day that Elisha passed over to Shunem, and a great woman [was] there, and she urged him to eat bread. And it was, as often as he passed by, he turned aside there to eat bread.
en.B: One day Elisha went on to Shunem. A wealthy woman lived there, and she pressed him to stay for a meal. After that, whenever he passed that way, he would stop there to eat.
en.R: One day Elisha went to the town of Shunem. A rich and important woman lived there. She begged him to come and eat a meal at her house. After that, every time he came through Shunem, he stopped there to eat.

decisions.choice: a great woman: a woman of wealth and standing
decisions.reason: "Great" describes a person's wealth and position, as with Nabal (1 Samuel 25:2) and Barzillai (2 Samuel 19:33). The rest of the story bears it out: she has a house large enough to add a room, servants, donkeys, and needs no favors from the king (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Shunem: a town in the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: Shunem lay in the land of Issachar, across the valley from Mount Gilboa (Joshua 19:18; 1 Samuel 28:4). Abishag came from there (1 Kings 1:3). Mount Carmel, where Elisha often stayed, was a long day's ride to the west (verse 25).

decisions.choice: eat bread: have a meal
decisions.reason: "Bread" stands for food in general; to eat bread is to share a meal.

decisions.choice: took hold on him: urged him strongly
decisions.reason: The verb means to grasp or be firm. Here she insists on her invitation, as a host would in that culture (Genesis 19:3; Judges 19:4).

decisions.choice: wealthy (Balanced); rich and important (Readable)
decisions.reason: "A great woman" would suggest fame or goodness to an English reader. Balanced and Readable give the sense of meaning decision m1.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־אִישָׁ֔הּ הִנֵּה־נָ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֛י אִ֥ישׁ אֱלֹהִ֖ים קָד֣וֹשׁ ה֑וּא עֹבֵ֥ר עָלֵ֖ינוּ תָּמִֽיד׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said to her husband, Look, please, I know that a holy man of God [is] he, passing over to us continually.

en.L: And she said to her husband, "Look, please, I know that he [is] a holy man of God who passes by us continually.
en.B: She said to her husband, "Listen, I am sure that this man who keeps coming our way is a holy man of God.
en.R: She said to her husband, "I am sure that this man who stops here so often is a holy man of God.

decisions.choice: holy: set apart for God and close to him
decisions.reason: "Holy" means belonging to God and set apart for him. She sees that Elisha is no ordinary guest. The word also hints at the danger of nearness to holiness that the widow of Zarephath felt (1 Kings 17:18).

decisions.choice: passing by us continually: he travels this way regularly
decisions.reason: The participle with "continually" describes a regular habit: Shunem lay on Elisha's usual route.

decisions.choice: Listen
decisions.reason: The word that calls attention (often "behold") is "listen" in Balanced; Readable leaves it out.

source.text: נַֽעֲשֶׂה־נָּ֤א עֲלִיַּת־קִיר֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְנָשִׂ֨ים ל֥וֹ שָׁ֛ם מִטָּ֥ה וְשֻׁלְחָ֖ן וְכִסֵּ֣א וּמְנוֹרָ֑ה וְהָיָ֛ה בְּבֹא֥וֹ אֵלֵ֖ינוּ יָס֥וּר שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: Let us make, please, an upper room of wall, small, and let us put for him there a bed and a table and a chair and a lampstand; and it will be, at his coming to us, he will turn aside there.

en.L: Please, let us make a small upper room with walls, and let us put a bed for him there, and a table and a chair and a lampstand. And it will be, when he comes to us, he can turn aside there."
en.B: Let us build a small room with walls on the roof and put a bed, a table, a chair and a lamp in it for him. Then whenever he comes to us, he can stay there."
en.R: Let us build a small, closed-in room for him on our roof. We can put a bed in it, and a table, a chair and a lamp. Then whenever he comes to visit us, he can stay there."

decisions.choice: an upper room with walls: a solid room built on the flat roof
alternatives: a small room on the wall
decisions.reason: Houses had flat roofs, and an upper room could be built on top, reached by an outside stair. "With walls" marks it as a lasting room, not a shelter of branches put up on the roof. Elijah had stayed in such a room in Zarephath (1 Kings 17:19).

decisions.choice: bed, table, chair and lampstand: a fully furnished guest room
decisions.reason: Many houses had few pieces of furniture. A bed, a table, a seat and a stand for an oil lamp made a comfortable private room where the prophet could rest, eat and read or pray at night.

decisions.choice: a small room with walls on the roof (Balanced); a small, closed-in room on our roof (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the room was; Readable says "closed-in" for "with walls".

decisions.choice: lamp
decisions.reason: The stand held a small oil lamp; Balanced and Readable say "lamp".

source.text: וַיְהִ֥י הַיּ֖וֹם וַיָּ֣בֹא שָׁ֑מָּה וַיָּ֥סַר אֶל־הָעֲלִיָּ֖ה וַיִּשְׁכַּב־שָֽׁמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And it happened one day, and he came there and turned aside to the upper room and lay down there.

en.L: And it happened one day that he came there, and he turned aside to the upper room and lay down there.
en.B: One day Elisha came there, went into the upstairs room and lay down there.
en.R: One day Elisha came to Shunem. He went into the room upstairs and lay down to rest.

decisions.choice: turned aside: went into, to stay
decisions.reason: The verb means to turn off the road; here it is to go in and stay, as the woman had planned (verse 10).

decisions.choice: upstairs room (Balanced); room upstairs (Readable)
decisions.reason: The same wordings as 1 Kings 17:19, where Elijah stays in an upper room.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־גֵּחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ קְרָ֖א לַשּׁוּנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֑את וַיִּקְרָא־לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לְפָנָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Gehazi his young man, Call this Shunammite. And he called her, and she stood before him.

en.L: And he said to Gehazi his young man, "Call this Shunammite." And he called her, and she stood before him.
en.B: He said to his servant Gehazi, "Call the Shunammite woman." So he called her, and she came and stood before him.
en.R: Elisha told his servant Gehazi, "Ask the woman from Shunem to come here." So Gehazi called her, and she came and stood before him.

decisions.choice: his young man: his servant
decisions.reason: The word means a young man, and often a servant or attendant (1 Kings 18:43). Gehazi, named here for the first time, is Elisha's personal servant.

decisions.choice: before him: in Elisha's presence
decisions.reason: She stands before Elisha, yet he speaks to her through Gehazi (verse 13), as a man of standing might do. The words could also mean that she stood before Gehazi.

decisions.choice: servant; the Shunammite woman (Balanced); the woman from Shunem (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "servant" for "young man", and explain "Shunammite".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֱמָר־נָ֣א אֵלֶיהָ֮ הִנֵּ֣ה חָרַ֣דְתְּ׀אֵלֵינוּ֮ אֶת־כָּל־הַחֲרָדָ֣ה הַזֹּאת֒ מֶ֚ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֔ךְ הֲיֵ֤שׁ לְדַבֶּר־לָךְ֙ אֶל־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ א֖וֹ אֶל־שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמִּ֖י אָנֹכִ֥י יֹשָֽׁבֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Say, please, to her, Look, you have been anxious for us [with] all this anxiety; what [is there] to do for you? Is there to speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army? And she said, In the midst of my people I [am] dwelling.

en.L: And he said to him, "Say, please, to her, 'Look, you have taken all this trouble for us. What [is there] to do for you? Is there [something] to speak on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?'" And she said, "I am living among my own people."
en.B: Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tell her, 'You have gone to all this trouble for us. What can be done for you? Can we speak for you to the king or to the commander of the army?'" She answered, "I live among my own people."
en.R: Elisha told Gehazi, "Say to her, 'You have taken so much care of us. What can we do for you in return? Do you want us to speak to the king or the army commander for you?'" She answered, "I have my own family around me. I do not need anything."

decisions.choice: you have been anxious for us with all this anxiety: you have taken great care over us
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to tremble. Here it describes anxious, careful attention to a guest's needs.

decisions.choice: speak for you to the king or the commander: Elisha had influence at court
decisions.reason: Elisha had dealings with the king of Israel (3:11-19). He offers to plead her case or win her a favor from those in power.

decisions.choice: I live among my own people: I am secure in my own clan
decisions.reason: She has relatives around her to protect and help her, so she needs no powerful patron. It is a polite refusal. Later, when she has lost her land, she does go to the king (8:1-6).

decisions.choice: commander of the army (Balanced); army commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wordings for this officer.

decisions.choice: I have my own family around me. I do not need anything.
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom with the sense of meaning decision m3.

source.text: וַיֹּ֕אמֶר וּמֶ֖ה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת לָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר גֵּיחֲזִ֗י אֲבָ֛ל בֵּ֥ן אֵֽין־לָ֖הּ וְאִישָׁ֥הּ זָקֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, And what to do for her? And said Gehazi, Truly, a son there is not to her, and her husband [is] old.

en.L: And he said, "Then what [is there] to do for her?" And Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband [is] old."
en.B: Elisha asked, "What then can be done for her?" Gehazi answered, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is old."
en.R: Elisha asked Gehazi, "So what can we do for her?" Gehazi answered, "She has no son, and her husband is old."

decisions.choice: no son and an old husband: no heir and little hope of one
decisions.reason: A son carried on the family name and inheritance and cared for his mother in old age. With an elderly husband, she had little hope of one, as with Sarah and Abraham (Genesis 18:11-12).

decisions.choice: truly: "well", introducing what Gehazi has noticed
decisions.reason: The word affirms what follows; Gehazi points out something Elisha may not have seen.

source.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר קְרָא־לָ֑הּ וַיִּקְרָא־לָ֔הּ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד בַּפָּֽתַח׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Call her. And he called her, and she stood in the doorway.

en.L: And he said, "Call her." And he called her, and she stood in the doorway.
en.B: Elisha said, "Call her." So Gehazi called her, and she stood in the doorway.
en.R: Elisha said, "Call her back here." So Gehazi called her, and she came and stood at the door of the room.

decisions.choice: she stood in the doorway: a sign of respect
decisions.reason: She stays at the entrance of the prophet's room and does not come in.

decisions.choice: Elisha ... Gehazi
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, since the Hebrew only says "he".

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אַ֖תְּ חֹבֶ֣קֶת בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֗אמֶר אַל־אֲדֹנִי֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים אַל־תְּכַזֵּ֖ב בְּשִׁפְחָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, At this appointed time, at the time [of] life, you [will be] embracing a son. And she said, No, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your maidservant.

en.L: And he said, "At this season, at the time [of] life, you [will be] embracing a son." And she said, "No, my lord, man of God, do not lie to your maidservant."
en.B: Elisha said, "About this time next year you will be holding a son in your arms." She said, "No, my lord, man of God! Do not deceive your servant."
en.R: Elisha said, "About this time next year you will be holding your own baby son in your arms." She said, "No, sir! Man of God, do not lie to me!"

decisions.choice: at this season, at the time of life: when this time comes round again, a year from now
decisions.reason: "The time of life" means the time when the year comes back to life, that is, the same season next year.

decisions.choice: the promise to Sarah
decisions.reason: The same words are used when Yahweh promises Abraham that Sarah will have a son (Genesis 18:10, 14). As with Sarah, the woman is childless and her husband old, and she cannot believe it.

decisions.choice: embracing a son: holding her own child
decisions.reason: She will hold her baby in her arms. Her answer, "do not lie", shows how deeply she wanted a son and how much she feared a false hope (verse 28).

decisions.choice: my lord ... your maidservant: polite address and humble self-reference
decisions.reason: As in verse 2, a woman of standing still speaks humbly to the man of God.

decisions.choice: deceive your servant (Balanced); lie to me (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "your servant" for the polite self-reference, as in verse 2, and Readable says "me"; Readable says "sir" for "my lord".

decisions.choice: about this time next year
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom in plain words.

source.text: וַתַּ֥הַר הָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן לַמּוֹעֵ֤ד הַזֶּה֙ כָּעֵ֣ת חַיָּ֔ה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר אֵלֶ֖יהָ אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

records.literal_gloss: And conceived the woman and bore a son at this appointed time, at the time [of] life, which spoke to her Elisha.

en.L: And the woman conceived and bore a son at this season, at the time [of] life, which Elisha had spoken to her.
en.B: But the woman conceived, and at that same season the following year she gave birth to a son, as Elisha had told her.
en.R: And the woman did become pregnant. About a year later she had a baby boy, just as Elisha had told her.

decisions.choice: at this season, at the time of life: the same words as the promise
decisions.reason: The narrator repeats the exact words of verse 16 to show that the promise was kept to the letter.

decisions.choice: at that same season the following year (Balanced); about a year later (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 16, Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom.

source.text: וַיִּגְדַּ֖ל הַיָּ֑לֶד וַיְהִ֣י הַיּ֔וֹם וַיֵּצֵ֥א אֶל־אָבִ֖יו אֶל־הַקֹּצְרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And grew the child, and it happened one day, and he went out to his father to the reapers.

en.L: And the child grew. And it happened one day that he went out to his father, to the reapers.
en.B: The child grew. And one day he went out to join his father among the reapers.
en.R: The boy grew older. One day he went out to the field where his father was working with the men who were harvesting the grain.

decisions.choice: the reapers: workers cutting the grain at harvest
decisions.reason: Grain was cut with sickles in the hot weeks of late spring and early summer. The scene sets the boy out in the fields in the heat of the day.

decisions.choice: to join his father among the reapers (Balanced); the men who were harvesting the grain (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the father was; Readable explains "reapers".

source.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר אֶל־אָבִ֖יו רֹאשִׁ֣י׀רֹאשִׁ֑י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־הַנַּ֔עַר שָׂאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־אִמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to his father, My head, my head! And he said to the young man, Carry him to his mother.

en.L: And he said to his father, "My head, my head!" And he said to the young man, "Carry him to his mother."
en.B: He said to his father, "My head! My head!" His father told a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
en.R: The boy cried out to his father, "My head hurts! My head hurts!" His father told a servant, "Carry him home to his mother."

decisions.choice: my head, my head: a sudden, severe pain
decisions.reason: The text does not say what was wrong. The harvest heat suggests sunstroke, but the point is that a sudden illness took the boy within hours (verse 20).

decisions.choice: the young man: a servant working in the field
decisions.reason: This is one of the father's workers, not Gehazi.

decisions.choice: My head hurts; home
decisions.reason: Readable says what the cry means and where the servant is to take him.

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂאֵ֔הוּ וַיְבִיאֵ֖הוּ אֶל־אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֧שֶׁב עַל־בִּרְכֶּ֛יהָ עַד־הַֽצָּהֳרַ֖יִם וַיָּמֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: And he carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until the noon, and he died.

en.L: And he carried him and brought him to his mother, and he sat on her knees until noon, and he died.
en.B: The servant picked him up and took him to his mother. He sat on her lap until noon, and then he died.
en.R: The servant carried him home. The boy sat on his mother's lap until noon, and then he died.

decisions.choice: on her knees: on her lap
decisions.reason: She held the sick child on her lap through the morning.

decisions.choice: until noon: he died within half a day
decisions.reason: The boy had gone out in the morning; by midday he was dead.

decisions.choice: the servant ... the boy
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who carried and who sat, since the Hebrew uses only "he".

source.text: וַתַּ֨עַל֙ וַתַּשְׁכִּבֵ֔הוּ עַל־מִטַּ֖ת אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתִּסְגֹּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went up and laid him on [the] bed of the man of God, and shut behind him and went out.

en.L: And she went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, and she shut [the door] behind him and went out.
en.B: She went upstairs and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut the door on him, and went out.
en.R: She carried him upstairs and laid him on the bed in Elisha's room. Then she shut the door and went out.

decisions.choice: the bed of the man of God: in the room she had made for Elisha
decisions.reason: She lays her son in the prophet's own room and on his bed, and tells no one. Her act already looks to the man of God for help, as the widow's son was laid on Elijah's bed (1 Kings 17:19).

decisions.choice: shut: the door
decisions.reason: The object is understood; she closes the door of the upper room.

decisions.choice: the door
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply "door"; Readable says "Elisha's room" for the bed of the man of God.

source.text: וַתִּקְרָא֮ אֶל־אִישָׁהּ֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר שִׁלְחָ֨ה נָ֥א לִי֙ אֶחָ֣ד מִן־הַנְּעָרִ֔ים וְאַחַ֖ת הָאֲתֹנ֑וֹת וְאָר֛וּצָה עַד־אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים וְאָשֽׁוּבָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And she called to her husband and said, Send, please, to me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, and I will run to the man of God and return.

en.L: And she called to her husband and said, "Please send me one of the young men and one of the donkeys, so that I may hurry to the man of God and come back."
en.B: She called her husband and said, "Please send me a servant and one of the donkeys. I want to hurry to the man of God and come straight back."
en.R: She called to her husband, "Please send me one of the servants and a donkey. I need to go quickly to the man of God. I will come right back."

decisions.choice: the donkeys: female donkeys used for riding
decisions.reason: The word is feminine. Female donkeys were valued riding animals, a sign of a well-off household (Judges 5:10; 1 Samuel 9:3).

decisions.choice: run: go in haste
decisions.reason: She will ride, not run on foot; the verb stresses speed.

decisions.choice: she says nothing of the boy's death
decisions.reason: She asks only for help to travel. She keeps the news for the man of God alone (verses 23, 26-28).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Young men" here are the household's servants (as in verse 12).

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר מַ֠דּוּעַ אַ֣תְּ הֹלֶ֤כֶת אֵלָיו֙ הַיּ֔וֹם לֹֽא־חֹ֖דֶשׁ וְלֹ֣א שַׁבָּ֑ת וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Why [are] you going to him today? Not new moon and not sabbath. And she said, Peace.

en.L: And he said, "Why [are] you going to him today? [It is] not new moon and not sabbath." And she said, "[It is] well."
en.B: He asked, "Why go to him today? It is neither a new moon nor a Sabbath." "It is all right," she said.
en.R: Her husband asked, "Why do you want to go to him today? It is not a New Moon festival or a Sabbath day." She answered, "It is all right."

decisions.choice: new moon and sabbath: holy days when people might visit a prophet
decisions.reason: The first day of each month and the seventh day of each week were days of rest and worship (Numbers 28:9-15; Amos 8:5). On such days people might go to a man of God. Her husband sees no reason for a visit on an ordinary working day.

decisions.choice: peace: "it is all right", a reply that sets the question aside
decisions.reason: The word means wholeness and well-being, and is the common greeting. Said alone as an answer, it means "all is well" or "never mind". She does not tell her husband the boy is dead; she will say it only to the man of God. The same word recurs in verse 26.

decisions.choice: [It is] well (Literal); It is all right (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The word usually rendered "peace" is here a short reply. "Peace" alone would not be understood as an answer, so Literal says "[it is] well" and Balanced and Readable "it is all right".

decisions.choice: New Moon festival; Sabbath day
decisions.reason: Readable adds "festival" and "day" so the young reader sees these were holy days.

source.text: וַֽתַּחֲבֹשׁ֙ הָֽאָת֔וֹן וַתֹּ֥אמֶר אֶֽל־נַעֲרָ֖הּ נְהַ֣ג וָלֵ֑ךְ אַל־תַּעֲצָר־לִ֣י לִרְכֹּ֔ב כִּ֖י אִם־אָמַ֥רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And she saddled the donkey and said to her young man, Drive and go; do not hold back for me [in] riding unless I say to you.

en.L: And she saddled the donkey and said to her young man, "Drive [it] and go; do not slow the riding for me unless I tell you."
en.B: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, "Drive on and go! Do not slow down for my sake unless I tell you."
en.R: She put a saddle on the donkey and told her servant, "Make the donkey go fast! Do not slow down for me unless I tell you to."

decisions.choice: drive: the servant goes on foot, urging the donkey on
decisions.reason: She rode while the servant walked or ran behind, driving the animal.

decisions.choice: do not hold back the riding: keep up the pace
decisions.reason: She wants no pause on the way.

decisions.choice: Make the donkey go fast
decisions.reason: Readable says what "drive" means here.

source.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ וַתָּב֛וֹא אֶל־אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל־הַ֣ר הַכַּרְמֶ֑ל וַ֠יְהִי כִּרְא֨וֹת אִישׁ־הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים אֹתָהּ֙ מִנֶּ֔גֶד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־גֵּיחֲזִ֣י נַעֲר֔וֹ הִנֵּ֖ה הַשּׁוּנַמִּ֥ית הַלָּֽז׃

records.literal_gloss: And she went and came to the man of God, to Mount Carmel. And it happened, when saw the man of God her from opposite, and he said to Gehazi his young man, Look, the Shunammite, that one.

en.L: And she went and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. And it happened, when the man of God saw her from a distance, that he said to Gehazi his young man, "Look, there [is] that Shunammite.
en.B: So she set off and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. As soon as the man of God saw her in the distance, he said to Gehazi his servant, "Look, there is the Shunammite woman.
en.R: So she left and went to the man of God at Mount Carmel. Elisha saw her coming while she was still far away. He said to his servant Gehazi, "Look! There is the woman from Shunem.

decisions.choice: Mount Carmel: the ridge by the sea, some 25 miles from Shunem
decisions.reason: Carmel runs to the Mediterranean on the west side of the Jezreel valley. Elijah had met the prophets of Baal there (1 Kings 18:19-20), and Elisha went there after Elijah was taken (2 Kings 2:25). The ride took most of a day.

decisions.choice: that one: pointing to her
decisions.reason: The word points at someone in view: "that woman over there".

decisions.choice: Elisha
decisions.reason: Readable names Elisha for "the man of God" in the second clause, so the reader can follow who sees her.

source.text: עַתָּה֮ רֽוּץ־נָ֣א לִקְרָאתָהּ֒ וֶאֱמָר־לָ֗הּ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לָ֛ךְ הֲשָׁל֥וֹם לְאִישֵׁ֖ךְ הֲשָׁל֣וֹם לַיָּ֑לֶד וַתֹּ֖אמֶר שָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Now run, please, to meet her and say to her, Is it peace to you? Is it peace to your husband? Is it peace to the child? And she said, Peace.

en.L: Now run, please, to meet her, and say to her, 'Is it well with you? Is it well with your husband? Is it well with the child?'" And she said, "[It is] well."
en.B: Run now to meet her and ask her, 'Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is the child all right?'" She answered, "It is all right."
en.R: Run and meet her. Ask her, 'Are you all right? Are your husband and your child all right?'" She answered, "Everything is all right."

decisions.choice: is it peace: are you well? Is all well?
decisions.reason: To ask about someone's "peace" is to ask after their welfare (Genesis 29:6; 2 Samuel 18:29). Elisha senses something is wrong and asks about each member of the family.

decisions.choice: her answer "well" puts Gehazi off
decisions.reason: As with her husband (verse 23), she gives the short answer and keeps her grief for Elisha himself (verse 27).

decisions.choice: Is it well with ... (Literal); Are you all right ... It is all right (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, the word usually rendered "peace" is here a question and answer about welfare.

source.text: וַתָּבֹ֞א אֶל־אִ֤ישׁ הָֽאֱלֹהִים֙ אֶל־הָהָ֔ר וַֽתַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּרַגְלָ֑יו וַיִּגַּ֨שׁ גֵּֽיחֲזִ֜י לְהָדְפָ֗הּ וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֤ים הַרְפֵּֽה־לָהּ֙ כִּֽי־נַפְשָׁ֣הּ מָֽרָה־לָ֔הּ וַֽיהוָה֙ הֶעְלִ֣ים מִמֶּ֔נִּי וְלֹ֥א הִגִּ֖יד לִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she came to the man of God to the mountain, and she took hold of his feet, and drew near Gehazi to push her away, and said the man of God, Let her alone, for her soul [is] bitter to her, and Yahweh has hidden from me and not told me.

en.L: And she came to the man of God at the mountain and took hold of his feet. And Gehazi came near to push her away, but the man of God said, "Let her alone, for her soul [is] bitter within her, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has hidden [it] from me and has not told me."
en.B: When she reached the man of God on the mountain, she clung to his feet. Gehazi came up to push her away, but the man of God said, "Let her be! She is in deep distress. {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has hidden it from me and not told me."
en.R: When she came to the man of God on the mountain, she grabbed hold of his feet. Gehazi came to push her away. But Elisha said, "Leave her alone! She is in terrible pain. And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has not let me know what is wrong."

decisions.choice: took hold of his feet: the act of a desperate petitioner
decisions.reason: Clinging to someone's feet was a way of begging for help with the whole self. Gehazi thinks it improper and tries to move her.

decisions.choice: her soul is bitter within her: she is in deep anguish
decisions.reason: "Bitter of soul" describes grief and distress, as with Hannah (1 Samuel 1:10) and David's men at Ziklag (1 Samuel 30:6).

decisions.choice: Yahweh has hidden it from me: the prophet knows only what Yahweh shows him
decisions.reason: Elisha does not know everything. He knows what Yahweh reveals, and this time he has been told nothing.

decisions.choice: She is in deep distress (Balanced); She is in terrible pain (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the idiom; "soul" here is the person's inner self.

source.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הֲשָׁאַ֥לְתִּי בֵ֖ן מֵאֵ֣ת אֲדֹנִ֑י הֲלֹ֣א אָמַ֔רְתִּי לֹ֥א תַשְׁלֶ֖ה אֹתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And she said, Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, Do not lead me astray?

en.L: And she said, "Did I ask a son from my lord? Did I not say, 'Do not mislead me'?"
en.B: She said, "Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, 'Do not mislead me'?"
en.R: She said, "Sir, I never asked you for a son! I told you, 'Do not give me false hope!'"

decisions.choice: mislead: lead on with a false hope
decisions.reason: This is a different verb from "lie" in verse 16. It means to lull or lead someone on. To be given a son and then lose him is worse than never to have had one.

decisions.choice: two questions that are charges
decisions.reason: Both questions expect the answer she has already given: she never asked for a son, and she did warn him. In this way she tells him the boy is dead without saying it.

decisions.choice: statements for questions
decisions.reason: Readable turns the questions into the statements they imply, and says "give me false hope" for "mislead me"; it says "sir" for "my lord".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לְגֵיחֲזִ֜י חֲגֹ֣ר מָתְנֶ֗יךָ וְקַ֨ח מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֣י בְיָדְךָ֮ וָלֵךְ֒ כִּֽי־תִמְצָ֥א אִישׁ֙ לֹ֣א תְבָרְכֶ֔נּוּ וְכִֽי־יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ אִ֖ישׁ לֹ֣א תַעֲנֶנּ֑וּ וְשַׂמְתָּ֥ מִשְׁעַנְתִּ֖י עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַנָּֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to Gehazi, Gird your loins and take my staff in your hand and go; if you meet a man, do not bless him, and if blesses you a man, do not answer him; and put my staff on [the] face of the boy.

en.L: And he said to Gehazi, "Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, do not greet {{gender:them|him}}, and if anyone greets you, do not answer {{gender:them|him}}. And lay my staff on the face of the boy."
en.B: Elisha said to Gehazi, "Tuck your robe into your belt, take my staff in your hand, and be on your way. If you meet anyone, do not greet {{gender:them|him}}, and if anyone greets you, do not answer. Lay my staff on the boy's face."
en.R: Elisha told Gehazi, "Get ready to go quickly. Take my walking stick and hurry. If you meet anyone on the way, do not stop to greet {{gender:them|him}}. If anyone greets you, do not even answer. Lay my stick on the boy's face."

decisions.choice: gird your loins: tuck up your robe to move fast
decisions.reason: Men wore long robes and tucked them into the belt to run or work (1 Kings 18:46).

decisions.choice: do not greet anyone: let nothing delay you
decisions.reason: The word for greeting is "bless". Greetings on the road were long exchanges of blessings and news. Gehazi is to go straight there.

decisions.choice: my staff: the prophet's staff, standing for his authority
decisions.reason: A staff could stand for the authority of the one who carried it, as Moses' staff did (Exodus 4:17). Elisha sends it ahead in Gehazi's hand, but it brings no life (verse 31).

decisions.choice: Tuck your robe into your belt (Balanced); Get ready to go quickly (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced explains the idiom as 1 Kings 18:46 does; Readable gives its purpose. Readable says "walking stick" for "staff".

decisions.choice: anyone ... them
decisions.reason: "Anyone" means any person, man or woman, so the pronoun takes the gender setting.

source.text: וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵ֣ם הַנַּ֔עַר חַי־יְהוָ֥ה וְחֵֽי־נַפְשְׁךָ֖ אִם־אֶעֶזְבֶ֑ךָּ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אַחֲרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said [the] mother of the boy, [As] lives Yahweh and [as] lives your soul, if I leave you. And he arose and went after her.

en.L: And the mother of the boy said, "[As] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and [as] your soul lives, I will not leave you." So he arose and went after her.
en.B: But the boy's mother said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave you." So Elisha got up and followed her.
en.R: But the boy's mother said, "As surely as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lives and as surely as you live, I will not leave without you!" So Elisha got up and went with her.

decisions.choice: as Yahweh lives and as your soul lives, if I leave you: a solemn oath that she will not leave
decisions.reason: An oath was sworn by the life of Yahweh and of the person addressed (1 Samuel 20:3; 25:26). "If I leave you" is the short form of an oath, meaning "I will certainly not leave you".

decisions.choice: Elisha's own oath to Elijah
decisions.reason: Elisha swore these same words three times when Elijah tried to leave him behind (2 Kings 2:2, 4, 6). Now the woman clings to Elisha as he clung to Elijah. She wants the prophet himself, not his staff or his servant.

decisions.choice: your soul lives: you yourself live
decisions.reason: "Soul" here is the living person.

decisions.choice: As surely as ... lives and as surely as you live
decisions.reason: The usual wording for this oath, as in 1 Samuel 25:26; Readable says "leave without you" for the sense.

source.text: וְגֵחֲזִ֞י עָבַ֣ר לִפְנֵיהֶ֗ם וַיָּ֤שֶׂם אֶת־הַמִּשְׁעֶ֨נֶת֙ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הַנַּ֔עַר וְאֵ֥ין ק֖וֹל וְאֵ֣ין קָ֑שֶׁב וַיָּ֤שָׁב לִקְרָאתוֹ֙ וַיַּגֶּד־ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֥א הֵקִ֖יץ הַנָּֽעַר׃

records.literal_gloss: And Gehazi passed on before them and put the staff on [the] face of the boy, and there was no voice and no attention; and he returned to meet him and told him, saying, Not awakened the boy.

en.L: And Gehazi passed on before them and laid the staff on the face of the boy, but [there was] no voice and no attention. And he returned to meet him and told him, saying, "The boy has not awakened."
en.B: Gehazi went ahead of them and put the staff on the boy's face. But there was no sound and no response. So he came back to meet Elisha and reported, "The boy has not woken up."
en.R: Gehazi went on ahead of them and laid the stick on the boy's face. But the boy did not make a sound or move. So Gehazi turned back, met Elisha on the way, and told him, "The boy has not woken up."

decisions.choice: no voice and no attention: no sound and no sign of response
decisions.reason: The boy did not answer or stir; he was still dead.

decisions.choice: the silence after the prophets of Baal called
decisions.reason: The same words describe the silence when the prophets of Baal cried to their god on Carmel: "no voice ... no attention" (1 Kings 18:29). The staff in Gehazi's hand does nothing; life will come only through prayer to Yahweh (verse 33).

decisions.choice: awakened: come back to life
decisions.reason: Gehazi speaks of death as sleep, a gentle way of saying the boy is still dead.

decisions.choice: Elisha
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elisha, whom Gehazi goes back to meet.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א אֱלִישָׁ֖ע הַבָּ֑יְתָה וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנַּ֨עַר֙ מֵ֔ת מֻשְׁכָּ֖ב עַל־מִטָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And came Elisha to the house, and look, the boy [was] dead, laid on his bed.

en.L: And Elisha came into the house, and look, the boy [was] dead, laid on his bed.
en.B: When Elisha reached the house, there was the boy, dead, lying on his bed.
en.R: When Elisha arrived at the house, he found the boy lying dead on the bed in his room.

decisions.choice: his bed: Elisha's own bed
decisions.reason: The mother had laid the boy on the bed of the man of God (verse 21).

decisions.choice: look, the boy was dead: the scene through Elisha's eyes
decisions.reason: "Look" lets the reader see what Elisha saw as he came in.

decisions.choice: the bed in his room
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that it was the bed in Elisha's own room.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּסְגֹּ֥ר הַדֶּ֖לֶת בְּעַ֣ד שְׁנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיִּתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went in and shut the door behind the two of them, and prayed to Yahweh.

en.L: And he went in and shut the door behind the two of them, and he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: He went in, shut the door on the two of them, and prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: He went into the room and shut the door, so that only he and the boy were inside. Then he prayed to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: he shut the door behind the two of them: alone with the child, as Elijah was
decisions.reason: Elijah carried the widow's son to his own room, away from his mother, and called on Yahweh (1 Kings 17:19-20). As with the oil (verses 4-5), the miracle happens behind a closed door.

decisions.choice: he prayed to Yahweh: life comes from Yahweh, not from the prophet or his staff
decisions.reason: The staff had failed (verse 31). Elisha's first act is to pray.

decisions.choice: so that only he and the boy were inside
decisions.reason: Readable spells out "the two of them".

source.text: וַיַּ֜עַל וַיִּשְׁכַּ֣ב עַל־הַיֶּ֗לֶד וַיָּשֶׂם֩ פִּ֨יו עַל־פִּ֜יו וְעֵינָ֤יו עַל־עֵינָיו֙ וְכַפָּ֣יו עַל־כַּפָּ֔יו וַיִּגְהַ֖ר עָלָ֑יו וַיָּ֖חָם בְּשַׂ֥ר הַיָּֽלֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: And he went up and lay on the child and put his mouth on his mouth and his eyes on his eyes and his palms on his palms, and he bent over him, and became warm [the] flesh of the child.

en.L: And he went up and lay on the child, and put his mouth on his mouth, and his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. And he bent down over him, and the flesh of the child became warm.
en.B: Then he got up on the bed and lay on the child, putting his mouth on the child's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hands on his hands. As he stretched himself out over him, the boy's body grew warm.
en.R: Then he climbed onto the bed and lay down on the boy. He put his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on the boy's eyes, and his hands on the boy's hands. As he stretched his body out over the boy, the boy's body began to get warm.

decisions.choice: Elisha does what Elijah did for the widow's son
decisions.reason: Elijah stretched himself out on the dead child three times and called to Yahweh (1 Kings 17:21). Elisha, who asked for a double share of Elijah's spirit (2 Kings 2:9, 15), does the same, covering the child's whole body with his own. The verb here is a different one, meaning to bend or crouch low.

decisions.choice: bent down over him: crouched over the child, covering him
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Elijah bending to the ground on Carmel (1 Kings 18:42). Here, with mouth on mouth and hands on hands, it means Elisha lay curled over the boy, his whole body over the child's.

decisions.choice: the flesh of the child became warm: life began to return
decisions.reason: The warmth is the first sign of life. The return of life comes in stages (verse 35).

decisions.choice: stretched himself out over him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable echo the wording of 1 Kings 17:21 to bring out the link with Elijah; Literal keeps "bent down" for the different verb. Both describe Elisha's body laid over the child.

decisions.choice: the child's ... the boy's
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the child where the Hebrew repeats "his", so it is clear whose mouth and eyes are meant.

source.text: וַיָּ֜שָׁב וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בַּבַּ֗יִת אַחַ֥ת הֵ֨נָּה֙ וְאַחַ֣ת הֵ֔נָּה וַיַּ֖עַל וַיִּגְהַ֣ר עָלָ֑יו וַיְזוֹרֵ֤ר הַנַּ֨עַר֙ עַד־שֶׁ֣בַע פְּעָמִ֔ים וַיִּפְקַ֥ח הַנַּ֖עַר אֶת־עֵינָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he returned and walked in the house once here and once there, and he went up and bent over him; and sneezed the boy seven times, and opened the boy his eyes.

en.L: And he turned back and walked in the house once this way and once that way, and went up and bent down over him. And the boy sneezed seven times, and the boy opened his eyes.
en.B: Elisha got down and walked back and forth in the house, then went up and stretched himself out over him again. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
en.R: Then Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the house. He went back to the bed and stretched himself out over the boy again. Then the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

decisions.choice: walked back and forth: waiting and praying
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. Elisha is not done; he waits and then goes back to the child.

decisions.choice: sneezed: breath came back into him
decisions.reason: This verb appears only here. The sneezes show that breath had returned to the body.

decisions.choice: seven times: complete restoration
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness; the boy is fully restored to life.

decisions.choice: stretched himself out over him again
decisions.reason: As in verse 34; "again" is supplied because this is the second time.

source.text: וַיִּקְרָ֣א אֶל־גֵּיחֲזִ֗י וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ קְרָא֙ אֶל־הַשֻּׁנַמִּ֣ית הַזֹּ֔את וַיִּקְרָאֶ֖הָ וַתָּב֣וֹא אֵלָ֑יו וַיֹּ֖אמֶר שְׂאִ֥י בְנֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he called to Gehazi and said, Call this Shunammite. And he called her, and she came to him, and he said, Take up your son.

en.L: And he called to Gehazi and said, "Call this Shunammite." And he called her, and she came to him. And he said, "Take up your son."
en.B: Elisha called Gehazi and told him, "Call the Shunammite woman." Gehazi called her, and when she came in, Elisha said, "Pick up your son."
en.R: Elisha called Gehazi and told him, "Call the woman from Shunem." So Gehazi called her. When she came in, Elisha said, "Here is your son. Pick him up."

decisions.choice: take up your son: the son given back, as in Elijah's day
decisions.reason: Elijah gave the boy back to his mother with "See, your son is alive" (1 Kings 17:23). Here Elisha's words are fewer still; the living boy speaks for itself.

decisions.choice: call this Shunammite: the same words as verse 12
decisions.reason: The story returns to its beginning: the woman is called to the prophet, now to receive her son a second time.

decisions.choice: Here is your son
decisions.reason: Readable adds a few words so the moment is clear.

source.text: וַתָּבֹא֙ וַתִּפֹּ֣ל עַל־רַגְלָ֔יו וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָ֑רְצָה וַתִּשָּׂ֥א אֶת־בְּנָ֖הּ וַתֵּצֵֽא׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And she came and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground, and she took up her son and went out.

en.L: And she came and fell at his feet and bowed down to the ground. And she took up her son and went out.
en.B: She came in, fell at his feet, and bowed low to the ground. Then she lifted up her son and went out.
en.R: She came in and fell down at Elisha's feet, bowing with her face to the ground. Then she picked her son up and went out.

decisions.choice: fell at his feet and bowed down: deep thanks and honor
decisions.reason: She says nothing. Earlier she took hold of his feet in grief (verse 27); now she falls at them in gratitude.

decisions.choice: with her face to the ground
decisions.reason: Readable shows what bowing to the ground looked like.

source.text: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֞ע שָׁ֤ב הַגִּלְגָּ֨לָה֙ וְהָרָעָ֣ב בָּאָ֔רֶץ וּבְנֵי֙ הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים יֹשְׁבִ֖ים לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְנַעֲר֗וֹ שְׁפֹת֙ הַסִּ֣יר הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וּבַשֵּׁ֥ל נָזִ֖יד לִבְנֵ֥י הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and the famine [was] in the land, and [the] sons of the prophets [were] sitting before him; and he said to his young man, Set the pot, the large, and boil stew for [the] sons of the prophets.

en.L: And Elisha returned to Gilgal, and the famine [was] in the land. And the sons of the prophets [were] sitting before him, and he said to his young man, "Put on the large pot, and boil stew for the sons of the prophets."
en.B: Elisha went back to Gilgal while there was a famine in the land. When the company of prophets were sitting before him, he said to his servant, "Put the large pot on the fire and cook some stew for the company of prophets."
en.R: Elisha went back to the town of Gilgal. At that time there was a famine in the land. Once, while the group of prophets was sitting with him to learn from him, he told his servant, "Put the big pot on the fire and make some stew for these prophets."

decisions.choice: Gilgal: probably the Gilgal in the hills near Bethel
decisions.reason: Elijah and Elisha set out from a Gilgal before going down to Bethel (2 Kings 2:1-2), so this seems to be a town in the hill country, not the Gilgal near the Jordan (Joshua 4:19). It cannot be certain which is meant.

decisions.choice: sitting before him: gathered as disciples to learn
decisions.reason: To sit before someone was to sit as pupils or followers before a teacher (Ezekiel 8:1; 2 Kings 6:1).

decisions.choice: the famine: a time of famine in the land
decisions.reason: The article may point to a famine the reader knows of, perhaps the seven years of 2 Kings 8:1. Food was scarce, which explains why wild plants were gathered (verse 39).

decisions.choice: sons of the prophets: the community of prophets
decisions.reason: As in verse 1.

decisions.choice: company of prophets (Balanced); group of prophets (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wordings; Readable adds "to learn from him" for the idiom of meaning decision m2.

source.text: וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֶחָ֣ד אֶל־הַשָּׂדֶה֮ לְלַקֵּ֣ט אֹרֹת֒ וַיִּמְצָא֙ גֶּ֣פֶן שָׂדֶ֔ה וַיְלַקֵּ֥ט מִמֶּ֛נּוּ פַּקֻּעֹ֥ת שָׂדֶ֖ה מְלֹ֣א בִגְד֑וֹ וַיָּבֹ֗א וַיְפַלַּ֛ח אֶל־סִ֥יר הַנָּזִ֖יד כִּֽי־לֹ֥א יָדָֽעוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went out one to the field to gather herbs, and found a vine of [the] field, and gathered from it gourds of [the] field, his garment full; and he came and sliced into [the] pot of the stew, for they did not know.

en.L: And one went out into the field to gather herbs, and he found a wild vine and gathered from it wild gourds, his garment full. And he came and sliced [them] into the pot of stew, for they did not know [them].
en.B: One of them went out into the fields to gather herbs. He found a wild vine and picked enough wild gourds from it to fill his cloak. He came back and sliced them into the pot of stew, though none of them knew what they were.
en.R: One of the prophets went out into the fields to find plants to eat. He found a wild vine and picked as many of its gourds as he could carry in his cloak. When he got back, he cut them up and put them into the pot of stew. None of them knew what kind of gourds they were.

decisions.choice: herbs: green plants for food
decisions.reason: The word is rare and its exact sense is unclear; it probably means edible greens or herbs gathered in the open country.

decisions.choice: wild gourds: the fruit of a wild vine, probably a bitter, poisonous kind
decisions.reason: The plant cannot be identified with certainty. It may be the colocynth, a creeping vine with small round gourds that are very bitter and act as a violent purge, harmful in quantity. The same word describes the gourd shapes carved in the temple (1 Kings 6:18).

decisions.choice: his garment full: carried in the fold of his cloak
decisions.reason: The outer garment, gathered up, served as a bag.

decisions.choice: they did not know: no one recognized the plant
decisions.reason: The object is understood: they did not know what the gourds were or that they were harmful.

decisions.choice: cloak
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the garment used to carry the gourds.

source.text: וַיִּֽצְק֥וּ לַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים לֶאֱכ֑וֹל וַ֠יְהִי כְּאָכְלָ֨ם מֵהַנָּזִ֜יד וְהֵ֣מָּה צָעָ֗קוּ וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ מָ֤וֶת בַּסִּיר֙ אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לֶאֱכֹֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And they poured out for the men to eat, and it was, as they ate from the stew, and they cried out and said, Death [is] in the pot, man of God! And they were not able to eat.

en.L: And they poured [it] out for the men to eat. And it happened, as they were eating from the stew, that they cried out and said, "Death [is] in the pot, man of God!" And they were not able to eat.
en.B: They served it out for the men to eat. But as they were eating the stew, they cried out, "Man of God, there is death in the pot!" They were not able to eat it.
en.R: They poured out the stew for the men to eat. But as soon as they tasted it, they shouted, "Man of God, there is death in the pot! It is poison!" So they could not eat it.

decisions.choice: death in the pot: the stew is deadly
decisions.reason: They cry that the food will kill them, probably warned by its bitter taste. They call to the man of God for help.

decisions.choice: they poured out: those who served
decisions.reason: The subject is general: whoever was serving the meal.

decisions.choice: It is poison!
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the cry "death in the pot" and adds what it means.

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ וּקְחוּ־קֶ֔מַח וַיַּשְׁלֵ֖ךְ אֶל־הַסִּ֑יר וַיֹּ֗אמֶר צַ֤ק לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ וְלֹ֥א הָיָ֛ה דָּבָ֥ר רָ֖ע בַּסִּֽיר׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said, Then take flour. And he threw into the pot and said, Pour out for the people, and let them eat. And there was not a harmful thing in the pot.

en.L: And he said, "Then bring flour." And he threw [it] into the pot and said, "Pour out for the people, and let them eat." And there was no harmful thing in the pot.
en.B: Elisha said, "Then bring some flour." He threw it into the pot and said, "Serve it to the people, and let them eat." And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
en.R: Elisha said, "Bring me some flour." He threw the flour into the pot and said, "Now serve it to the people so they can eat." And there was nothing harmful in the stew anymore.

decisions.choice: the flour: a sign, not a cure
decisions.reason: Flour could not make poison harmless. As with the salt thrown into the spring at Jericho (2 Kings 2:20-22), the act shows that Yahweh is at work through his prophet.

decisions.choice: a harmful thing: anything bad or dangerous
decisions.reason: "Bad thing" here means something that does harm.

decisions.choice: in the stew anymore
decisions.reason: Readable says "stew" for "pot" and adds "anymore" to show the change.

source.text: וְאִ֨ישׁ בָּ֜א מִבַּ֣עַל שָׁלִ֗שָׁה וַיָּבֵא֩ לְאִ֨ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים לֶ֤חֶם בִּכּוּרִים֙ עֶשְׂרִֽים־לֶ֣חֶם שְׂעֹרִ֔ים וְכַרְמֶ֖ל בְּצִקְלֹנ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר תֵּ֥ן לָעָ֖ם וְיֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought to the man of God bread of firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and fresh grain in his sack. And he said, Give to the people and let them eat.

en.L: And a man came from Baal-shalishah and brought the man of God bread of [the] firstfruits, twenty loaves of barley, and fresh grain in his sack. And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat."
en.B: A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing the man of God bread from the firstfruits: twenty loaves of barley bread, and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat."
en.R: A man came from the town of Baal-shalishah. He brought the man of God twenty loaves of barley bread, made from the first grain of the harvest. He also brought a bag of fresh heads of grain. Elisha said, "Give this food to the people so they can eat."

decisions.choice: bread of the firstfruits: from the first grain of the harvest
decisions.reason: The first of the harvest belonged to Yahweh and was given to the priests (Leviticus 23:17-20; Numbers 18:13; Deuteronomy 18:4). This man brings it to the man of God instead, perhaps because faithful people in the northern kingdom did not take their gifts to the priests Jeroboam had set up (1 Kings 12:31).

decisions.choice: fresh grain in his sack: new ears of grain in a bag
decisions.reason: "Fresh grain" is the new ears, which could be roasted and eaten (Leviticus 2:14; 23:14). The word for the bag appears only here; its exact sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Baal-shalishah: a town in the land of Shalishah
decisions.reason: Saul passed through the land of Shalishah looking for his father's donkeys (1 Samuel 9:4). It lay in the hill country of Ephraim, not far from Gilgal; its exact site is unknown.

decisions.choice: barley: the first grain to ripen and the cheaper bread
decisions.reason: Barley ripened before wheat, so it was the first harvest. Barley bread was the common food of ordinary people.

decisions.choice: Elisha
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Elisha as the one who gives the order; Readable explains "firstfruits" and "fresh grain".

source.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ מְשָׁ֣רְת֔וֹ מָ֚ה אֶתֵּ֣ן זֶ֔ה לִפְנֵ֖י מֵ֣אָה אִ֑ישׁ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תֵּ֤ן לָעָם֙ וְיֹאכֵ֔לוּ כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָכֹ֥ל וְהוֹתֵֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And said his attendant, How shall I set this before a hundred men? And he said, Give to the people and let them eat, for thus says Yahweh, Eating and leaving over.

en.L: And his attendant said, "How can I set this before a hundred men?" And he said, "Give to the people, and let them eat, for thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: 'Eating and leaving over.'"
en.B: His attendant said, "How can I set this in front of a hundred men?" But Elisha said, "Give it to the people to eat, for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says this: 'They will eat and have some left over.'"
en.R: His helper asked, "How can I feed a hundred men with this?" But Elisha said, "Give it to the people so they can eat. This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: 'They will eat, and there will be food left over.'"

decisions.choice: his attendant: one who served Elisha personally
decisions.reason: The word names a personal assistant, as Joshua was to Moses (Exodus 24:13) and Elisha to Elijah (1 Kings 19:21). The text does not say whether this is Gehazi.

decisions.choice: eating and leaving over: they will eat and have food left
decisions.reason: Yahweh's word is two short verb forms, a terse promise: there will be enough, and more.

decisions.choice: a hundred men: the community of prophets
decisions.reason: Twenty small barley loaves would feed only a few people; the attendant cannot see how they will feed a hundred.

decisions.choice: the LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wordings for this prophetic formula; Readable says "helper" for "attendant".

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֧ן לִפְנֵיהֶ֛ם וַיֹּאכְל֥וּ וַיּוֹתִ֖רוּ כִּדְבַ֥ר יְהוָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And he set before them, and they ate and left over, according to [the] word of Yahweh.

en.L: And he set [it] before them, and they ate and left [some] over, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: So he set it before them. They ate, and there was some left over, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.
en.R: So Elisha's helper set the food in front of them. They all ate, and there was food left over, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said.

decisions.choice: according to the word of Yahweh: the promise kept
decisions.reason: The account ends by stressing that what happened was what Yahweh had said through his prophet (verse 43).

decisions.choice: a few loaves feeding many, with some left over
decisions.reason: Jesus later fed great crowds with a few loaves, among them five barley loaves, and there were leftovers (Mark 6:41-44; John 6:9-13). This small feeding looks ahead to those.

decisions.choice: Elisha's helper; the food; all
decisions.reason: Readable names who served and what was served.
